headlines.headline: Futures slide into Thursday: Nasdaq 100 e-minis -1.93%, S&P 500 e-minis -1.1%, Dow e-minis -0.69% as of ~1:56 AM PT, as investors re-price AI spending after Tesla and Meta earnings and a rebound in oil sours sentiment.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tech-led futures selloff sets a weak cash-open tone; the AI-capex debate is now the tape's main driver.

headlines.headline: Q3: revenue $64.6B (+26% YoY) beat ~$63.3B est; EPS $3.83 beat ~$3.57 but carried a $9.89B one-time legal charge (Aug 2026 settlement with 52 state AGs over teen mental health; ex-charge EPS $7.40). Q4 revenue guided $73-76B vs ~$73.6B consensus; 2026 capex narrowed up to $135-145B. Board approved a new non-voting Class C share structure via conditional one-for-one stock dividend. Q3 capex was $34.9B and free cash flow turned negative at -$2.12B. Shares jumped 2-6% after hours, then slipped ~1.9% premarket on the share issuance and AI-cost scrutiny.
headlines.why_it_matters: Revenue beat plus solid guide is a sentiment tailwind, but funding the AI build with new equity while FCF goes negative shifts the debate from growth to financing, capping the pop.

headlines.headline: Q3: revenue $28.05B flat YoY, adjusted EPS $0.48 beat ~$0.44; operating income fell 56% to $718M as opex rose 39% on AI/robotics; auto revenue fell 3% to $20.56B; free cash flow swung to +$1.53B vs an expected ~$4.5B burn. Management cut 2026 capex guidance to ~$20B (from $25B+) and gave a slower Optimus timeline (external deliveries around end-2027). Shares down ~5.3% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The headline beat came from spending less, not selling more; the capex cut reads as the Optimus/AI ramp slipping, which is the bearish signal the stock is pricing.

headlines.why_it_matters: Record results being sold on guidance confirms the regime: the market is grading the AI cycle on future spend, not past beats.

analysis: The theme of this tape is the AI capex bill coming due. Meta and Tesla both beat revenue and EPS, and the market punished the spending story in both, just in opposite directions: Meta is funding the build with new non-voting equity while its quarterly capex exceeded operating cash flow for the first time and FCF went negative, so the after-hours pop faded into a premarket decline; Tesla spent $3.2B less than expected and cut the 2026 guide by ~$5B, which reads as the Optimus/AI ramp slipping rather than discipline, and the stock fell 5%+. Lam Research getting sold on record results for soft guidance is the third data point: this market is grading guidance, not results. That is a sharp turn from yesterday's 4 AM brief, which carried META/TSLA estimates and had futures green (ES +0.22%); both prints are now known and futures are red across the board (ES -1.1%, NQ -1.93%). Oil near five-month highs adds a macro headwind and pulled the 10Y down to ~5.085% on safety flows. The noise to discount: the NYT Iran-strike-plans item (secondhand, unconfirmed) and the Anthropic S-1 timing (single unnamed-source report); the WSB bearishness on both names is color, not new information.
